title: Custom IPS signature rules: export, validate and import wire behavior in the legacy API

checks.do: Whether an export call sends no CSV content type on the request, since the gateway answers 415 to it.
Whether validation posts an object with a ruleText key, and whether a failure is read from the HTTP status and error envelope rather than a result body.
Whether anything depends on the CSV import path, which the Go SDK ships disabled and whose wire behavior is unconfirmed.
Whether a category list read is complete, by checking which SDK read it.
Whether a Python create was stopped by the pre-flight validation, which returns an error value without calling create, and that an update is not validated first.

export-request-no-csv-type.statement: The Go export function documents that the request must not advertise Content-Type text/csv: the OneAPI gateway rejects that with HTTP 415 on this body-less GET, and only application/json, the SDK default for GET, is accepted on the request side.

quotes: Important: the request itself MUST NOT advertise Content-Type: text/csv.
The OneAPI gateway rejects that with HTTP 415 Unsupported Media Type for
accepted on the request side.

export-response-raw-csv.statement: The export response is streamed as application/octet-stream with an attachment disposition, and the Go function returns the raw CSV bytes undecoded.

quotes: Content-Type: application/octet-stream and Content-Disposition: attachment;
// The response body is still raw CSV; ReadRaw does not decode it.

validate-body-wrapped.statement: The validate endpoint takes a JSON object with a ruleText key; the Go SDK states the API rejects a raw string payload.

quotes: string payloads; the rule text must be wrapped in this object.
JSON object ({"ruleText": "..."}) as required by the API and the response

validate-http-signaling.statement: Validation is signalled at the HTTP level: per the Go SDK comment a well-formed rule returns HTTP 200 with status 0 and empty error fields, and an invalid rule returns HTTP 400 with a standard error envelope (INVALID_INPUT_ARGUMENT and the diagnostic in message), which the SDK surfaces as an error rather than a populated struct.

quotes: rule returns HTTP 200 with status=0 and empty error fields. An invalid rule
returns HTTP 400 with a standard error envelope (INVALID_INPUT_ARGUMENT and
populated struct.

import-disabled.statement: The Go SDK ships the CSV import and import-status functions commented out, with a note that the export and import endpoints are currently broken upstream, kept as reference for when the backend is fixed.

import-csv-format.statement: The disabled import code documents the CSV as plus rows with five columns (rule name, rule text, category name, description and enable flag) and minus rows that carry only a rule name, which delete it; it says inner double quotes in the rule text must be doubled per RFC 4180 because the portal's parser rejects backslash-escaped quotes with 'Double quotes not terminated'.

categories-go-all-pages-python-one-page.statement: The Go IPS categories read pages through ReadAllPages, whereas the Python list_categories sends one request carrying the caller's page and page_size parameters.

quotes: err := common.ReadAllPages(ctx, service.Client, ipsCategoriesEndpoint, &ipsCategories)

python-create-preflight.statement: The Python `add_ips_signature_rule` validates the supplied `rule_text` through the validate endpoint before it sends the create, and on a failure returns `(None, None, ValueError(...))` without making the create call.

quotes: returns ``(None, None, ValueError(...))`` and no create call is made.
validation_error = self._preflight_validate_rule_text(kwargs)

python-update-no-preflight.statement: The Python `update_ips_signature_rule` does not validate `rule_text` first. Its docstring says the validate endpoint flags any signature whose `sid` already exists on the tenant as a duplicate, which on an update is the rule being changed, so a pre-flight check would reject every legitimate update.

quotes: Unlike :meth:`add_ips_signature_rule`, this method does **not** call
itself, so a pre-flight check would reject every legitimate update.

export-broken-note-vs-live-function.summary: One Go source file says the export and import endpoints are broken upstream, yet ships the export function live with detailed working-response handling.

quotes: // NOTE: The /ipsSignatureRules/{export,import} endpoints are currently broken

positions.says: Both export and import endpoints are broken upstream.

quotes: // Content-Type: application/octet-stream and Content-Disposition: attachment;

positions.says: The export function is live and describes the CSV it streams and the request header it must avoid.

export-broken-note-vs-live-function.impact: An agent cannot tell from the SDK whether export works on a current tenant; only the import path is tracked as open.

import-wire-unconfirmed.title: Whether CSV import works on current tenants and which multipart field name it expects
import-wire-unconfirmed.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the import and import-status functions are disabled in the Go SDK as broken upstream, and the multipart field name file is a guess with untested alternates; no source confirms current server behavior.
import-wire-unconfirmed.blocks: Whether bulk import of custom IPS signatures can be offered or scripted.
